lines.text: Even here is chilly in the morning.
River rafting fall covers the seas in the distance
and hugs the bases of tree-covered hills.
This world is at peace.
In silent resounds, choir chords calm the nerves of things I can't control
and offer them as keepsakes back to the higher powers.
Exhausted emotions carry forward a diminishing flame
to emit jazz tuned lyrics that heat and dry the morning dew.
All the remnants of the destruction revealed in the sunlight.
We can rebuild this temple.
It's a new day.
The catharsis evoked by loss in the painful crawl
along the cobblestone boulevards of broken dreams.
I can close a chapter and open a journal stored away
from moments of great clarity.
Words written from life's triumphs to offer a blueprint
of keeping faith alive and as majestic.
When words are read aloud and sung alone as gospels
to the lonely mirror's midnight hours,
the left tears drying with time that is common to past.
We can embrace a new day.
We can receive a new day.
We can welcome a new day.
Everything I've known and learned,
every circumference of life we're celebrating and believing
is here together in this sacred place,
reveling in the sunlight of a new beginning
with this world and a heart at peace.

scenes.lines: river-rafting fog / covers the seas in / the distance— / & hugs the bases of / tree covered hills— / this world is / at peace.
scenes.treatment: POET watches fog/haze drifts in off of undeveloped shoreline.

shots.action: The fog rafts in over the sea and wraps the bases of the tree-covered hills; the chapel ruin and the parked bike small on the shore
From behind POET at the ruined chapel wall: fog drifting in off the undeveloped shoreline toward him

bodies.action: stands at the broken wall, watching

shots.action: Fog passes across POET's face; he breathes out. This world is at peace.

scenes.lines: In silent resounds— / choir chords / calm the nerves / of things I can't control / & offer them / as keepsakes back to the / higher powers. / Exhausted emotions / carry forward / a diminishing flame / to emit jazz-tuned / lyrics / that heat / & dry / the morning dew / on the remnants of / the destruction / revealed / in the sunlight.
scenes.treatment: POET begins to rebuild a new temple, or rather it builds itself with POET. Temple is not old, but futuristic, modern, clean and white.

shots.action: Dawn comes up from the horizon; POET walks in among the chapel rubble, still dark in the valley, and stops where the platform will be
POET lifts both palms and the first white course of the platform arrives under them, dot by dot, and settles

bodies.action: raises his palms; the stone comes with them

shots.action: Three courses down; POET raises his arms on the struck note as the third settles; the sun dries the dew off the remnants of the chapel

scenes.lines: We can rebuild this temple. / It's a new day. / a catharsis— / evoked by loss / & the painful crawl / along the cobble-stone / boulevards of / broken dreams.
scenes.treatment: (Continues: the temple builds itself with POET.) Staged from the line: under sun rays, columns and beams go up.

shots.action: Sun rays cut through the air; six white columns rise one after another along the platform

bodies.action: walks the platform as the columns rise

shots.action: POET walks the stylobate behind the colonnade, each column taking him and each gap giving him back; a beam slides into place above
Morning dew on the new white stone winks in the light

scenes.lines: I can close / a chapter & open a / journal stored / away for moments / of great clarity— / words written / from life's triumphs / to offer a blueprint of / keeping faith / alive— / & it's majestic.
scenes.treatment: (Treatment silent; staged from the module line: laps around infinity pools of edgeless dreams that reflect the enormity of the skies; the journal from the poem line.)

shots.action: POET walks a lap along the edgeless pool; sky and sun mirrored whole beneath him

bodies.action: walks a lap, journal under his arm

shots.action: He sits at the pool's lip and opens the journal
Over his shoulder: handwritten pages, and the sky in the water beyond them

scenes.lines: when words / are read aloud— / & sung alone as / gospels to the lonely / mirror's / midnight hours— / that left tears / drying with time / that has come / & too passed—
scenes.treatment: (Treatment silent; staged from the module line: that we too can walk on water; deep breaths.)

shots.action: POET walks across the sea the whole width of the frame; the water goes flat and bright under his feet and nowhere else

bodies.action: walks on the water, reading aloud from the journal

shots.action: Tracking with him: he closes the journal and takes a deep breath; the stillness around him grows and shrinks with his breath
His shoes on the water: no ripple

scenes.lines: We can embrace a new day; / We can receive a new day; / We can welcome a new day. / Everything / I've known & / learned / every / circumference of life / worth celebrating / & believing / are here / together, in / this sacred place / reveling / in the sunlight / of a new beginning / with this world— / & a heart, / at peace.

bodies.action: stands in the arriving light, arms opening

shots.action: POET raises his arms in welcome beside the temple standing on the shoreline

bodies.action: raises both arms to the new day

passage.why_fulcrum: The turn from ruin to making: after the remnants in the sunlight, his first 'we' and first act. The rebuilt white temple becomes the hall that poem 12 fills, so this line sets what the next scene is.

answer.title: Fifteen Minutes in India
answer.said: Inside the temple, however, the stonework is severely plain.
answer.why: Same word in the same sense: a real temple, seen from inside. 'Severely plain' meets the bone-white, calm temple the scene book says he raises; a sober answer to his promise.

passage.gesture_detail: His right palm lowers and lies flat on the white stone coping of the pool, a builder's hand on the first stone; held still from before the line until the picture closes.
passage.surface: water: the reflecting pool in front of the portico; the archive picture opens in the reflection, edged by the stone coping.

plate.why: The White Temple and its Pools: a white portico across a reflecting pool among trees. Poem 11 has no generated plates; this view is the temple he rebuilds, and the pool is a real surface in it.

passage.staging: Locked wide on the portico across the pool. He stands at the near edge in profile facing the portico, palm on the coping; the pool's reflection becomes the archive picture after his line.
